title: Combine Failed and Succeeded Timelines
learning_objective: Learn how to put separate status tables into one labeled timeline.

tutorial.explanation: When statuses live in separate tables, normalize them into one stream with a label column before grouping intervals.
tutorial.syntax: SELECT 'failed' AS period_state, fail_date AS status_date FROM failed UNION ALL SELECT 'succeeded', success_date FROM succeeded;
tutorial.mental_model: UNION ALL stacks rows vertically. Adding a label preserves where each row came from.

guided_example.prompt: Create one timeline with period_state and status_date.
guided_example.solution_query: SELECT 'failed' AS period_state, fail_date AS status_date FROM failed UNION ALL SELECT 'succeeded' AS period_state, success_date AS status_date FROM succeeded;
guided_example.explanation: Each SELECT returns the same two columns, so UNION ALL can stack them.

practice.prompt: Return a combined timeline with period_state and status_date.
practice.expected_query: SELECT 'failed' AS period_state, fail_date AS status_date FROM failed UNION ALL SELECT 'succeeded' AS period_state, success_date AS status_date FROM succeeded;

hints: Both SELECT statements need the same columns.
Use UNION ALL, not a join.
